formationLabel: St. George Society incorporated April 26, 1911 · St. George Congregation formalized August 30, 1913 · cornerstone blessed November 30, 1913 · renamed St. Gabriel by 1918 · closed, exact date and mechanism unresolved; records run through 1997
currentUse: St. Gabriel Congregation is closed and its records are held by the Archdiocese of Milwaukee Archives. Its former 1913 church at the historic 5th-and-Lapham location, now identified as 1575 S. 10th Street/1000 W. Lapham Boulevard, remains standing. The current Archdiocese directory places Congregation of the Great Spirit at the same corner, supporting current Catholic use of the historic site/building. This is building reuse, not a canonical continuation or merger from St. Gabriel.
summary: St. Gabriel was Milwaukee's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish, initially organized under the name St. George. The April 26, 1911 event belongs to incorporation of the St. George Society, not the congregation. The St. George Congregation was formalized August 30, 1913, and its cornerstone was blessed November 30, 1913. The parish adopted the name St. Gabriel during its first pastor's tenure and was recorded under that name by 1918. Official Archdiocese sources identify the congregation as Lithuanian, place it at 5th and Lapham in the historical address system, list records through 1997, and classify it as closed/merged without naming a merger successor. The Wisconsin Historical Society identifies the former church at 1575 S. 10th Street as standing; the current Archdiocese directory places Congregation of the Great Spirit at 1000 W. Lapham Boulevard on the same corner. Institutional closure, archival custody, and later Catholic building use are modeled separately.

historicalNarrative.text: Milwaukee's Lithuanian Catholic organization began with the St. George Society. The visually reviewed Wolkovich text identifies April 26, 1911 as the society's incorporation. It separately records August 30, 1913 as formalization of the St. George Congregation. The dossier rejects the compendium shorthand that calls the 1911 act a congregation incorporation, because it collapses two legally and institutionally distinct milestones.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, vol. 3, PDF p. 46 / printed p. 38; society incorporation and congregation formalization

historicalNarrative.text: The new congregation's cornerstone was blessed November 30, 1913. During the first pastor's tenure the institution changed its name from St. George to St. Gabriel, and Wisconsin Historical Society documentation records the St. Gabriel name by 1918. An official Archdiocese sacramental-record list identifies St. Gabriel as a Lithuanian congregation founded in 1913 at 5th and Lapham, preserving the historic address form.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish endured severe early financial and governance disputes before the Archdiocese again called on Marian Fathers in the 1940s to stabilize it. Wolkovich records 610 parishioners of Lithuanian roots in a 1950 diocesan census and describes later immigrant cultural activity. Those facts demonstrate mid-century parish life but do not establish its terminal mechanism or current ethnic ministry.

historicalNarrative.text: Official Archdiocese sources establish closed status and archival custody without naming a successor or effective closure date. The closed/merged list includes St. Gabriel, and the archives collections page identifies MC 99, St. Gabriel Congregation records for 1916–1997. The dossier treats 1997 only as the end of the documented collection span, not proof of the parish's closure date, and does not invent a merger destination, suppression decree, or transfer of parish membership.

historicalNarrative.text: The church building survived the congregation. Wisconsin Historical Society identifies the former St. George/St. Gabriel church at 1575 S. 10th Street as not demolished and notes the related parsonage at 1575A. The current Archdiocese directory lists Congregation of the Great Spirit at 1000 W. Lapham Boulevard on the same 10th-and-Lapham corner. Together these sources support standing, current Catholic building use while leaving canonical succession expressly unclaimed.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The April 26, 1911 date belongs to incorporation of the St. George Society, not the congregation. August 30, 1913 is the congregation milestone and November 30, 1913 the cornerstone. Official evidence establishes closed status and records through 1997, but not an effective 1997 closure or specific merger successor. Historic 5th-and-Lapham and modern 10th/Lapham addresses are preserved rather than silently normalized.
